qt: to the Commission Nikolaos Anadiotis (NI) Subject:

Special education schools across the Greek territory are faced with a multitude of serious and chronic problems in terms of building, logistical and operational infrastructure, endangering the health and safety of pupils and teachers. Pupils with disabilities are housed in completely unsuitable and even dangerous conditions.1 Numerous cases of special schools housed in containers, former shops - or even active factory premises - have come to light. The premises do not meet hygiene requirements. Children with special needs are treated as second-class children by the State. All of the above, among other things, provoke strong protests from their parents. In light of the above, the Commission is asked: 1.
In the last decade, in Greece, has the Commission allocated funds for the improvement of existing buildings housing special schools or for the construction of new-build facilities or classrooms?
If so, are there official accounts or an implementation report on the allocation of these funds?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.9.2025) Over the last decade, Greece has received EU funding for both upgrading existing infrastructure and building new school facilities, including those for special education such as the construction of the special needs schools and kindergartens in Zakynthos1 and Korydallos2. Promoting equal access to inclusive and quality services in education, training and lifelong learning through developing accessible infrastructure constitutes a priority for 2021-2027 cohesion policy funding3, which is also reflected in the Greek Partnership Agreement 202120274. Through Greece’s 13 Regional Programmes, the EU has made around EUR 372 million available to Greece for upgrading and expanding infrastructure at all levels of education (early childhood, primary, secondary, tertiary and vocational education/training), investments that should promote inclusion and be prioritised according to a detailed mapping of needs. As per the Common Provisions Regulation5, cohesion policy investments benefitting persons with disabilities shall comply with United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities’ (UNCRPD) obligations and should not contribute to any form of segregation or exclusion, including ensuring infrastructure accessibility. Under the principle of shared management, selection and implementation of projects, including on special education infrastructure, is the responsibility of the Member State and the respective managing authorities. However, the Commission monitors closely the programmes’ implementation and works closely with the national authorities to ensure effective absorption of funds, in line with EU regulation and programme priorities.
